heading: 5. Core Profiles, Identifiers, And Conformance
text: 5. Core Profiles, Identifiers, And Conformance

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: A deployment claiming conformance to this BCP as a complete Logos module system MUST establish its initial Module Loader provider through protected, non-recursive bootstrap.

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: After Runtime binds that provider, it MUST use it to realize the orchestration module under protected bootstrap policy.

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: Every subsequent local module implementation MUST also be realized through the bound Module Loader provider.

heading: 5.1 Individual And Complete-System Conformance
text: Runtime MUST NOT substitute an independently started implementation or pre-existing provider endpoint for Module Loader realization.

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: 5.2 Profile Terminology

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: Its owner MUST define the profile's scope, required algorithms or mechanisms, validation rules, failure behavior, and relationship to other profiles.

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: An implementation MUST NOT replace a specification-fixed profile with another mechanism.

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: It also MUST NOT override an explicit deployment or request selection merely because it supports another profile.

heading: 5.2 Profile Terminology
text: Terms such as product profile, host profile, security profile, isolation profile, audit profile, or platform profile MUST NOT create independent Core selection layers merely by being named.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: The `Support requirement` column states what a conforming implementation must implement.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: Production remote transport | `logos.remote.quic` | Optional to implement. | Deployment or Runtime policy may select it only when both endpoints support it. Selection MUST be explicit.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: Package realization | `lgx` | Optional individually; a conforming Package Manager MUST implement at least one package realization profile. | A request selects it with `source.kind` equal to `"lgx"`.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: Package realization | `nix` | Optional individually; a conforming Package Manager MUST implement at least one package realization profile. | A request selects it with `source.kind` equal to `"nix"`.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: A conforming Package Manager MUST implement at least one of the `lgx` or `nix` realization profiles.

heading: 5.3 Defined Profile Matrix
text: Failure of a selected profile MUST NOT cause fallback to another profile unless the owning specification explicitly defines that fallback as safe.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: A complete deployment MUST document every applicable choice that the Core specifications assign to deployment. At minimum, that documentation MUST identify: … any selected presentation profile and its platform integration.

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements

heading: 5.4 Deployment Profile Requirements
text: It MUST NOT silently replace the selected behavior with a weaker mechanism.

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy.

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: The specification MUST define:

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … one stable identifier and its normative owner;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … the exact selection point and any default;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … whether support is mandatory, conditional, optional, development-only, or prohibited in production;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … the complete data schema, algorithms, validation rules, and failure behavior;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … how the profile composes with or excludes every related profile;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … downgrade, fallback, and unknown-profile behavior;

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A normative specification SHOULD introduce another named profile only when a complete interoperable behavior cannot be expressed by an existing profile, ordinary typed field, or local deployment policy. The specification MUST define: … the conformance tests or vectors needed for independent implementations.

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: A generic string, opaque byte string, configuration key, backend name, or policy label MUST NOT define a Core profile by itself.

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: They MUST NOT appear in addresses, discovery results, or negotiation fields defined by these specifications.

heading: 5.5 Rules For Additional Profiles
text: Unknown or unsupported profile identifiers MUST fail the dependent operation unless the owning specification explicitly permits the identifier to be ignored.
